standard.title: Evaluate movement strategies
standard.description: propose and evaluate movement strategies and skills that would be most effective in different movement situations
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have predicted and tested the effectiveness of different skills and strategies in a range of movement situations (Y5-6). They can make predictions and test them but have not yet been expected to systematically propose and evaluate across a range of situation types.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students propose and evaluate movement strategies and skills that would be most effective in different movement situations.

nodes.label: Proposing movement strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the key features of a movement situation and propose a strategy or skill selection that responds to those features with a stated rationale.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the key features of one movement situation and propose a strategy or skill most likely to be effective, giving one reason.
nodes.typical_width: Identify relevant contextual features across a range of movement situations; propose strategies and skills that respond to each; articulate the rationale for each proposal in terms of what the situation demands.
wider: Explain and justify the movement strategies selected in response to outdoor or nature-based activity challenges (rope courses, bushwalking, orienteering, canoeing) where environmental unpredictability is a key contextual feature
Investigate how movement strategy selection differs between competitive and cooperative movement contexts and what contextual features drive the differences
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluation requires a proposal to evaluate — students who cannot make reasoned proposals have no object for their evaluation. The quality of proposal reasoning determines whether evaluation is substantive or superficial.

response_modes.reason: Scaffold proposal reasoning by explicitly modelling situation analysis: what are the demands of this situation, what skills or strategies address those demands, and why? Build this as a consistent thinking routine before evaluation is introduced.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one key feature of a movement situation that informs strategy selection
Proposes a movement strategy or skill appropriate to that situation with a stated rationale

nodes.label: Testing and acting on proposals
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can put proposed movement solutions into action, predicting outcomes in advance and observing whether actual outcomes match predictions.
nodes.minimum_width: Implement a proposed movement strategy and describe whether the outcome matched what was predicted.
nodes.typical_width: Implement proposals across multiple movement situations; predict outcomes before each attempt; compare actual and predicted outcomes; identify what caused divergence where it occurred.
wider: Put movement solutions into action in outdoor or nature-based activity contexts where the environment introduces unexpected variables, and reflect on how predictions needed to be revised
Design a movement challenge that requires peers to propose a strategy before participating, then evaluate their proposals against actual outcomes

response_modes.reason: The propose-predict-test cycle builds through iteration — students need multiple rounds of testing proposals against outcomes to develop reliable prediction judgement.

success_criteria: Implements a proposed movement strategy in a physical activity
States a prediction about the outcome before implementation
Describes whether the actual outcome matched the prediction

nodes.label: Evaluating effectiveness and transfer potential
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the effectiveness of movement strategies across situations, identifying factors that enabled success and considering how successful approaches might transfer to other contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate whether a proposed strategy was effective and identify one factor that influenced the outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate strategy effectiveness across a range of situations; identify enabling and limiting factors; justify why certain strategies would transfer to other contexts and which would not; connect evaluation findings to future strategy selection.
wider: Evaluate factors that enabled success in movement activities and justify how these factors can be transferred to other learning contexts beyond HPE
Compare evaluate-and-transfer cycles across indoor game contexts and outdoor/nature activity contexts, examining which strategies proved most generalisable

response_modes.reason: Evaluation integrates proposal reasoning, testing experience and transfer judgement into one reflective capability. Instruction should keep the full cycle visible — evaluation is not a standalone final step but a return to proposal reasoning.
Transfer potential is only visible when students have evaluated across multiple situation types. Width in movement situation types is what makes transfer claims substantive rather than speculative.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Transfer evaluation is a genuinely metacognitive capability — students who can identify why a strategy worked in one context and whether it would work in another have developed analytical thinking that extends well beyond movement contexts.
success_criteria: Evaluates whether a proposed movement strategy was effective, with at least one reason
Identifies a factor that contributed to the outcome (positive or negative)
Makes a reasoned judgement about whether the strategy or skill could be transferred to a different movement context
